build.note: Read from saved raw captures; no export, no new capture.

question: What names the soldier-style target materials that L3370 and L3374 could not attribute, and what selects the 'against armor' material 579?

sourceFacts.method: All affector files with Armor in the name were decoded (affdump.py). Those of class Class_99b2c2df hold a list of material pairs (Field_4a94515c, Field_465fa50b) and a kind value; those of class Class_79520af1 hold entries of an integer, an amount and a factor. Every material the pairs name was read against five sample bullet materials in both level grids. A corrected file search (matusers2.py: every saved raw root, low byte 0x80 or 0x81) replaced the search used in L3370 and L3374, which covered three raw roots only and required the low 20 bits to equal 0x80.

control.description: The soldier file's packed materials 579 and 587 read as in L3370, and material 579 holds 0.84 / 0.91 / 0.67 against automatic, DMR and bolt-action bullets as EA's 1.3.3.0 notes state for the chest against armor.

sourceFacts.correction: L3370 said no other saved file names 579 or 587, and L3374 said no saved file names 13 further target materials. Both statements came from an incomplete search. The armor affectors name 579, 587, 586, 580, 581, 238, 239, 292, 394, 395, 419 and 421. Materials 74, 418, 420, 535 and 536 remain without a decoded user.

inference: Armor changes which material a hit is scored against. The soldier file gives 579 and 587; the soft armor affector maps 579 to 579 (no change) and its 'effective health' variant keeps 587, while the ceramic armor affector maps 579 to 238 and the ceramic variant maps head 587 to 586. That the first material of a pair is replaced by the second is read from this structure; the field names are hashes.

With soft armor the values are those of L3370: chest 0.84 / 0.91 / 0.67 (EA's 'against armor' line) and a head table with 2.25 for bolt-action bullets. With ceramic armor the head material 586 holds 1.75 for bolt-action bullets instead of 2.25, so ceramic armor lowers the bolt-action headshot; and the chest material 238 holds values above 1 (3.0 automatic, 3.8 DMR, 4.0 bolt-action), which cannot be damage to health and reads as damage to the plate. That last reading is a guess.
The firing range targets use the same mechanism (394, 395, 419, 421 mapped to material 3).
The amount affectors hold 40, 80, 121 and 242 with a factor 0.5. 40 and 80 fit armor amounts per vest tier; 121 and 242 (twice 121) are unexplained. None is recorded as an armor value.
Which game modes grant these upgrades is not in these files; EA's line sits in the general gunplay section.
unresolved: Armor amount per plate and what 121 / 242 mean. Test in a mode with armor: one assault rifle bullet to the chest of an armored enemy, reading health and armor lost.
Bolt-action headshot on an armored enemy: 2.25 times with soft armor, 1.75 with ceramic, by this reading.
Materials 74, 418, 420, 535 and 536 still have no decoded user.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Soldier armor is stored as material swaps: armor affectors name the chest material 579 and head material 587 and map them to other materials; this replaces L3370 and withdraws the dead end L3374
leads.summary: Soldier armor is stored as material swaps. The soldier file names a chest material 579 (EA's against-armor values 0.84 / 0.91 / 0.67) and a head material 587 (bolt-action 2.25); the ceramic armor affectors map them to 238 and 586 (bolt-action head 1.75), the soft armor affectors leave them. This replaces L3370's statement that nothing else names these materials and withdraws the dead end L3374, whose file search was incomplete. Armor amounts 40 and 80 appear in the vest affectors but are not confirmed. 202 raw-offset checks matched.
leads.reopenWhen: An in-game damage reading on an armored soldier.
leads.statusNote: Swap tables and grid values read; direction of the swap and the amounts are candidates.
